title: D-Wave Enhances Stride Hybrid Solver and Releases Applied Optimization Learning Path - Quantum Computing Report
gist: D-Wave upgraded its Stride hybrid solver, reporting large gains on traveling salesperson and assembly-line benchmarks, and launched a three-course optimization curriculum on Leap. The article also covers an FAU study in which a D-Wave annealing-based QSVM led a lung cancer classification benchmark.

insights.claim: D-Wave announced algorithmic upgrades to its Stride hybrid solver, which couples classical compute with its quantum annealing hardware and is available via the Leap cloud platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: D-Wave's commercial pitch rests on hybrid solvers rather than pure QPU performance.

insights.claim: On traveling salesperson problems up to 10,000 locations, the solver averaged within 0.02% of optimal in 15 seconds, over 200x closer to optimal than the prior Stride version at matched runtime.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vendor benchmark versus its own prior version, not versus leading classical solvers.

insights.claim: On TSP instances over 10,000 locations, Stride averaged within 3.8% of optimal in 120 seconds, over 500x closer to optimal than the prior solver generation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gains are relative to D-Wave's earlier solver, which sets a low baseline.

insights.claim: On assembly line balancing, the new Stride reached higher-quality solutions in 15 seconds than the previous version did in 120 seconds, with the article citing an eightfold speedup.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Manufacturing scheduling is a plausible commercial use case.

insights.claim: Stride partitions problem sub-graphs across classical computing clusters and quantum annealers, and the revision targets core solver architecture to shorten time-to-solution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Much of the improvement is classical algorithm engineering within a hybrid stack, which blurs attribution to quantum hardware.

insights.claim: Combinatorial optimization, spanning routing logistics, manufacturing scheduling and supply chain allocation, is described as one of the primary commercial applications for quantum annealing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Addressable market is in logistics and operations budgets.

insights.claim: D-Wave released a three-course developer curriculum, Applied Quantum Optimization, covering use-case formulation, mathematical modeling, QUBO formulation and deploying hybrid solvers in production software stacks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Education lowers adoption barriers and builds a developer base.

insights.claim: A Florida Atlantic University study in Discover Quantum Science evaluated quantum classifiers under intentionally restricted data, using QUBO feature selection to cut 16 clinical attributes to 10 symptoms and training on only 108 patient samples with 432 out-of-sample records for evaluation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small-data healthcare ML is a niche where quantum approaches are being tested.

insights.claim: An annealing-based QSVM on D-Wave Advantage_system6 (Zephyr topology) achieved 91.90% accuracy on hardware and 94.31% in simulation, the best across five software frameworks and both gate-based and annealing modalities, outperforming gate-based implementations in Qiskit, Cirq and PennyLane.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Third-party academic result favorable to D-Wave, though the dataset is small and no classical baseline is cited.

insights.claim: Against gate-based execution on an IBM quantum processor on a reduced 50-sample set, annealing completed hardware execution orders of magnitude faster due to lower circuit-shot overheads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Speed advantage reflects circuit-shot overhead, not necessarily accuracy superiority.
